meta: Edmund C. Tarbell's 1901 painting of his wife Emeline walking with a parasol on Bos'n's Hill in New Hampshire.
about: Edmund Tarbell's wife Emeline strolls across Bos'n's Hill with a parasol to keep off the sun, and a pet dog goes with her. The hill is in New Castle, New Hampshire, and was a favourite leisure spot for the family, which included four children. The museum says the place gives the picture its luminous setting. Tarbell painted it in 1901. Four years later the couple bought a summer house nearby. He was a popular art professor in Boston, and his followers were nicknamed Tarbellites.
credit_line: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Thomas A. Mann and Robert A. Mann

meta: Marguerite Gérard's Deserved Sorrows, painted in the late 1780s, shows a woman on a sofa beside a suit of armor.
about: A richly dressed woman reclines on a gold upholstered sofa next to a suit of armor and a sword. At the left a servant in a brown bodice holds a tray with a glass and a golden ewer, and an oval portrait of a man hangs on the paneled wall above. Marguerite Gérard painted it in the late 1780s as one of a pair. It was on the Swiss art market in 1978. The National Gallery of Art bought it in 2025 from a Paris dealer.
credit_line: Gift of Edwin L. Cox – Ed Cox Foundation, Chester Dale Fund, and Patrons' Permanent Fund

meta: Giorgione's Giovanni Borgherini and His Tutor, a double portrait with a Latin motto on a scroll, now in Washington.
about: Latin letters on a scroll in a young man's hand say that talent has no worth unless accomplishment follows. He also holds an armillary sphere, and a figure in a gold garment points toward him. Vasari wrote in 1568 that the Borgherini sons in Florence owned a Giorgione portrait of Giovanni as a young man in Venice, with his tutor beside him, and this may be that picture. Doubts remain about the attribution, because the painting has no recorded history before the 20th century. Michael Straight gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1974.

meta: A porcelain copy by Elise de Maussion after Paul Delaroche's The Virgin at the Foot of the Cross.
about: Kneeling beside a tall wooden cross, a veiled woman in a grey mantle presses one hand against the beam and lifts her face in grief. Soft grey tones stand out against a deep blue ground scattered with gold stars. This is a copy of Paul Delaroche's composition, painted on porcelain by Elise de Maussion and monogrammed E. de M. at lower left. A damaged label on the back says she made it herself. It was later in the collection of Régine Deforges, and a Paris dealer sold it in 2022.

meta: Aertgen Claesz van Leyden's 1520 Saint Jerome in his study, lost in thought over a skull by candlelight.
about: Saint Jerome sits lost in thought in his study at night, staring at the skull he holds in his left hand. A candle burns beside him, a cardinal's hat and a rosary hang on the wall, and an hourglass stands on a small shelf above. An open book and an inkwell lie on the table. Aertgen Claesz van Leyden painted it in 1520. In the late 17th century it was listed at Ham House near London as a work by Lucas van Leyden. The Rijksmuseum bought it from an Amsterdam dealer in 1956.

meta: Jan Boeckhorst's Saint Martin Dividing His Cloak, painted in the 1640s, once sold as a work by Van Dyck.
about: An armored rider on a white horse draws his sword and cuts his red cloak in two, offering half to a nearly nude beggar who kneels beneath a stone archway. Onlookers crowd in, among them a woman with a small child, and a city with a tall tower shows through the arch. Jan Boeckhorst painted it in the 1640s. Sold as a Van Dyck in Paris and again in Orléans, it later belonged to Cardinal Joseph Fesch and then to the Holford family in London. Andrew Mellon bought it, and his daughter left it to the National Gallery of Art in 1970.

meta: Giovanni Gerolamo Savoldo's Saint Matthew and the Angel, a night scene from about 1530 to 1535 in the Metropolitan Museum.
about: Saint Matthew sits at a writing table by candlelight and looks up at an angel in blue drapery who stands behind him. A moonlit arch opens at the left, and at the right a small scene of figures around a fire is visible. Giovanni Gerolamo Savoldo painted it around 1530 to 1535, and it is one of the night scenes he is best known for. Wikipedia says it was a major influence on the young Caravaggio. X-rays show a drawing of a woman on the right half.

meta: A mid-1500s hanging scroll landscape with a poem, bearing the seal of Kano Motonobu.
about: Mist covers the mountain behind a river, with a small pavilion on the near shore and a tiny boat on the water. The large red tripod-shaped seal is that of Kano Motonobu, head of the Kano school atelier in Kyoto that served the shogun. The Zen monk Gesshū Jukei of the Kenninji temple wrote the poem, which tells of a friend who rows over reciting verse and plans to drink with the speaker at an inn on the river. The museum thinks the scroll was likely a gift to a respected associate, perhaps someone weary of the politics of the capital.
credit_line: Gift from the Collection of George Gund III

meta: Joseph Blackburn's 1756 portrait A Military Officer, a man in a red coat inside a painted oval.
about: Under a white powdered wig, a man turns slightly toward us with a faint smile. He wears a red coat with dark blue facings and gold buttons over a cream waistcoat, set against a dark olive ground inside a painted oval. Joseph Blackburn signed and dated the spandrel at lower left in 1756. In 1924 the portrait was shown in New York as General Joshua Winslow, but the National Gallery lists the sitter only as a military officer. Thomas B. Clarke owned it, and the A. W. Mellon Trust gave it to the Gallery in 1947.

meta: Matteo di Giovanni's panel of the Madonna and Child with angels and cherubim, painted in the 1460s on a gold ground.
about: The Virgin holds the nude Christ Child on her lap, in a dark blue mantle over a red dress, and he reaches for her hand. Angels with gold halos crowd behind them against gold leaf, and two small cherubim sit at lower right. Latin letters on her halo read, O Queen of Heaven, rejoice. Matteo di Giovanni painted the panel in the 1460s. It possibly hung in the Ashburnham collection in England and went to the dealer Duveen in 1919. Andrew Mellon's trust bought it, and it was given to the National Gallery of Art in 1937.
dimensions:
painted surface: 69.7 x 49.5 cm (27 7/16 x 19 1/2 in.)
overall size: 79 x 58 cm (31 1/8 x 22 13/16 in.)
framed: 99.7 x 78.1 x 8.3 cm (39 1/4 x 30 3/4 x 3 1/4 in.)

meta: J. C. Leyendecker's 1918 Weapons for Liberty, a Lady Liberty and a kneeling Boy Scout, made for a magazine cover.
about: Lady Liberty stands in a star-patterned cloak above a kneeling Boy Scout who holds a sword engraved with the words Be Prepared. A large shield with an eagle seal rises behind them against pale mountains, with USA Bonds across the top and Weapons for Liberty on a banner below. J. C. Leyendecker painted it in oil in 1918, and it first appeared on a magazine cover. It was then reused as a poster for the Boy Scouts of America's Third Liberty Loan campaign.

meta: Merry Joseph Blondel's study of Venus healing the wounded Aeneas, from Virgil's Aeneid, made around 1820.
about: Aeneas, wounded in battle, has dragged himself away, and Venus, his mother, comes to heal him inside a divine mist. The river god Numicus holds the hero while she pours a healing balm from a golden vessel. A cupid clings to her. Merry Joseph Blondel made this as a study for a larger painting of a scene from Virgil's poem, around 1820. It was sold from the collection of Hippolyte Lebas at the Hôtel Drouot in Paris in 1867, and the Art Institute of Chicago bought it in 2015.
credit_line: Purchased with funds provided by Pamela and Roger Hull through the Old Masters Society

meta: Simone Martini's Saint Matthew, a half-length gold-ground panel from a series of ten saints.
about: Saint Matthew appears half-length inside an arched frame, a quill in one hand and an inkwell on an open red book in the other. His halo is gilded, the ground is gold, and the letters SCS MATHEV are written beside him. The panel belonged to a series of ten saints that the Cologne collector Johann Anton Ramboux bought in Italy, and it was sold in 1867 under the name of Lippo Memmi. Philip Lehman owned it by 1928, and the Kress Foundation bought it in 1943.
dimensions:
painted surface: 26.4 x 19.6 cm (10 3/8 x 7 11/16 in.)
overall: 30.8 x 23.2 cm (12 1/8 x 9 1/8 in.)
framed: 44.4 x 60 cm (17 1/2 x 23 5/8 in.)

meta: John William Casilear's Lake George, a view of islands and mountains painted after 1851.
about: Low wooded islands lie scattered across a broad lake that holds the reflection of a pale, cloud-filled sky. Mountains recede in layers at the left. A leafy tree and dense foliage frame the right side and the foreground. John William Casilear painted this view of Lake George after 1851. His niece Josephine Harrison gave it to the Corcoran Gallery of Art in Washington in 1897, and the National Gallery of Art acquired it from that collection in 2014.
credit_line: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Josephine E. Harrison, 1897)

meta: A letter changes hands in a music room in Nicolas Delaunay's 1770 print Le Billet Doux, after Niclas Lafrensen the younger.
about: A letter is passing from a standing man to a seated woman, who reaches toward him with a small musical instrument in her lap. A second woman at the left reads a sheet of music. A harp and a cello stand to the right beside a harpsichord. Books and a box lie on the floor. The room is ornate, with a large mirror over the mantel, a patterned carpet, wall sculptures and garlands. A cat sits by the fireplace. Nicolas Delaunay made the print in 1770 after a gouache by Niclas Lafrensen the younger.

meta: Cornelis Ketel's 1574 round portrait of a man probably Adam Wachendorff, with a putto blowing bubbles on the back.
about: In a round panel, a man in black with a white ruff stands with one hand on his hip and a folded letter in the other. On the table beside him lie paper, a pen, an inkwell and a watch. The sitter is probably Adam Wachendorff, and the inscription gives his age as 35. Cornelis Ketel dated the portrait 1574. On the back he painted a naked putto blowing bubbles in a landscape. The frame carries a Latin motto saying that the word of God is eternal and everything else passes. The Rijksmuseum received it through the De Bruijn-van der Leeuw Bequest.

meta: Thomas Hicks's 1830 portrait of his cousin Edward Hicks at work on a Peaceable Kingdom.
about: Seated at ease with a palette and brush, a man looks out at us beside an easel that holds a landscape with animals and small figures. He is Edward Hicks, a Quaker minister from Bucks County, Pennsylvania, who earned part of his income by painting signs and coaches. His cousin Thomas Hicks painted him in 1830 at work on one of the hundred or so versions of The Peaceable Kingdom he made. The pacifist theme comes from a prophecy of Isaiah about the wolf living with the lamb. Hicks sold, traded or gave his pictures to neighbors.

meta: C. R. W. Nevinson's 1913 painting The Arrival, a steamship entering a harbour in Futurist fragments.
about: Fragments of a steamship entering a harbour are broken into angular planes and swirling smoke, and the word Transatlantic can be read on its hull. Several people are visible. C. R. W. Nevinson painted it in 1913 from different viewpoints at once, and Wikipedia reads it as a sign of his interest in the Futurist movement. When it was shown in 1915 it carried another title, My Arrival in Dunkirk. The artist's widow gave it to Tate Britain in 1956.

meta: Joseph Badger's 1755 portrait of a white-haired captain with a dark hat, painted on bed ticking.
about: Resting one hand on a carved stone pedestal and holding a dark hat in the other, a white-haired man in a gray coat looks out from the canvas. He wears a white cravat and lace cuffs. Joseph Badger painted the captain in 1755 on bed ticking, a woven cloth, and put the date at lower right. The portrait stayed with the Buffum family of Walpole, New Hampshire, until 1943. Edgar William and Bernice Chrysler Garbisch bought it in Boston and gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1957.
credit_line: Gift of Edgar William and Bernice Chrysler Garbisch
